verdict.summary: A normal multi-tenant AI agent is ineligible under Strava's published API Policy: it prohibits using Strava API Materials or Strava Data to develop, train, evaluate, or operate an AI Application, including grounding, embeddings, and RAG. Strava MCP is the sole authorized agent-mediated interface, but is limited to subscribers' personal use of their own data and may not enable commercial or third-party access. The published policy documents no public-OAuth exception for this use case.
verdict.activeEffort: 15 hours–4 days (sum of the step estimates below). Not applicable for a policy-compliant normal multi-tenant AI integration; do not implement the integration under the published policy.
verdict.waitTime: Not applicable to the AI-policy blocker. The published 7–10-business-day target applies to ordinary Developer Program review, not a documented exception to the AI Application prohibition.
verdict.mainGate: The published AI Application prohibition blocks the proposed use case; ordinary Developer Program capacity review does not override that prohibition.

recommendation.text: Do not ship a public-OAuth Strava integration for this multi-tenant AI agent. Ask Strava for written authorization describing the AI operation, data flow, model providers, retention, tenant isolation, and commercial distribution; absent that authorization, exclude Strava from the agent. Do not build an alternate MCP server or use Strava MCP for commercial or third-party access.

essentials.text: Use server-side authorization-code exchange at POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token. Access tokens expire after six hours; persist the replacement refresh token atomically because every successful token request immediately invalidates the prior refresh token. Keep access and refresh tokens separately, and bind each credential set to its individual athlete/tenant connection.

sources.quote: The application must now call the POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token with its client ID and client secret to exchange the authorization code for a refresh token and short-lived access token.
Access tokens expire six hours after they are created, so they must be refreshed in order for an application to maintain access to a user's resources.
Once a new refresh token is returned, the older refresh token is invalidated immediately.
In general, we recommend storing short-lived access tokens and refresh tokens in separate tables

detail.text: Do not proceed with a production multi-tenant AI integration under the published policy, which prohibits operating an AI Application with Strava API Materials or Strava Data. You may contact Strava to ask whether any exception, partner agreement, or alternative permitted architecture exists, but the published documentation does not establish a written-authorization path.

steps.title: Prepare a tenant-safe OAuth callback design

detail.text: Implement a confidential server-side authorization-code callback with state validation, server-side exchange, per-athlete credential storage, and granted-scope checks; do not expose the client secret.

sources.quote: Redirect the user to GET https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize .
Must be code .

steps.output:
Callback rules:
1. Create cryptographically random state tied to tenant, user, nonce, and expiry.
2. Redirect only to https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize with response_type=code.
3. On callback, verify state before reading code.
4. Exchange code server-side only; never expose client_secret.
5. Encrypt tokens at rest per athlete connection.
6. Atomically replace refresh_token on refresh.
7. Persist granted scopes; disable features the athlete declined.
